jobs.prompt:
You are job OS (OASIS, T17 Orb v2 character sketches). You cannot run code or see images; the coordinator runs your script with Python 3.12 + Pillow and looks at the PNGs.
Braden's direction: a pixel-art coworker with a SCREEN FACE, on a transparent background, with a two-button bar under it (a pencil/write icon and a voice waveform placeholder icon, in one rounded dark pill with a thin divider). It must be an ORIGINAL OASIS character: NOT a robot with a cloud head (the style reference is a blue robot whose head is a puffy cloud with a '>_' screen face; do not reuse that silhouette), not a copy of any other product's assistant or mascot (no Clippy-like paperclip, no Android-like robot, no known game or brand character). Friendly and calm; it lives in the corner of the screen of a non-technical office worker at Cluer Holdings. OASIS means a small green refuge in a desert: you may use that idea, but no palm-tree clichés required.
Write exactly one file: coordination/references/orb-sketches/make_sketches.py. It defines THREE clearly different characters (different silhouettes, not recolors), each as a list of equal-length strings (one char per pixel, '.' = transparent) plus a palette dict char -> '#RRGGBB'. Canvas per character: 32 wide x 36 tall for the body, then the button bar drawn below it as pixel art too (about 26 x 9 px, same palette style), total at most 32 x 48. Each screen face shows a simple expression made of lit pixels (eyes/prompt glyph). Use crisp outlines (1 px darker edge), 2-3 shades per material, a limited palette (max 10 colours per character).
The script, when run from the oasis root: for each character writes coordination/references/orb-sketches/sketch-<n>-<slug>.png upscaled 8x with nearest-neighbour on a TRANSPARENT background (RGBA), and also writes contact-sheet.png: the three side by side at 6x, each shown once on #1E1E1E and once on #F2F2F2 (two rows), with a 16 px gap. It asserts every row of a grid has the same width and every char is in the palette, and prints one line per file written. Standard library + Pillow only. No network.
Also include at the top of the script a docstring with one line per sketch: number, name, slug, one-sentence idea, why it is not a cloud-head robot or a known mascot.
End with one JSON line: {"files_changed":[...],"sketches":[{"n":1,"name":"...","idea":"..."}, ...]}.
